en: Unlike temperate countries with four seasons, the Philippines only experiences two main seasons: the dry and wet seasons.
Mount Apo is the highest mountain in the Philippines, whereas Mount Pulag is only the third highest.
The Cagayan River, not the Pasig River, is the longest and largest river in the Philippines.
Laguna de Bay, not Lake Lanao, is the largest lake in the Philippines by surface area.
Unlike most volcanoes on land, Taal Volcano's main crater is situated on an island inside Taal Lake.
Mayon Volcano is famous for its perfectly symmetrical cone shape, not a flat summit like a table mountain.
Unlike countries in the Southern Hemisphere, the entire Philippine archipelago is located north of the equator.
Palawan belongs to the Mimaropa region in the Luzon island group, not the Visayas.
The Tubbataha Reefs are located in the center of the Sulu Sea, far from the Palawan coast.
The Chocolate Hills are formed from uplifted marine limestone and coral deposits, not from volcanic activity.
The Sierra Madre mountain range runs along the eastern coast of Luzon, not the island of Mindanao.
The Philippine Sea is located on the eastern side of the archipelago, not the western side.
